correctness.rationale: Verified from the primary signed-filter definition that the chain hull has exactly n+1 affinely independent u,v_k vertices. Reconstructed every facet a_k,b from vertices, norms N_{n-k}, and positive dependency b+sum 2^(k-1)a_k=0; for any inball (c,r), summing facet-clearance inequalities proves r<=2^n/(N_{n-1}+sum 2^(k-1)N_{n-k}). The facet-equality linear system attains that bound uniquely, yielding the asserted incenter coordinates. Bisector equations give q_j=1/2-2^-j; all vertices lie at squared distance n/4+4/3-2^-n-4^-n/3. q is in ordinary chain order polytope, hence in their enriched hull, so convex contact weights and parallel-axis identity prove the unique minimum enclosing sphere. Checked n=1 endpoint and asymptotic n->infinity. Independently recovered facets via matrix inversion, solved Chebyshev LP and exact circumcenters and nonnegative barycentric contact weights for n=1..10; finite checks only corroborate universal proof. Source verify.py uses floating-point inradius checks (contrary to prose claim of exact symbolic checks), but the analytic derivation does not rely on those tests.
residual_risks: Independent numerical inradius replay limited to n<=10 and not a stand-in for general proof; exact symbolic circumcenter and facet checks cover those tested n only.

value.rationale: The chain gives a canonical, geometrically natural family of all-dimensional reflexive simplices, and the inball and minimum enclosing ball are natural metric invariants rather than arbitrary finite slices. The explicit pair of centers/radii and sharp aspect ratio n^(3/2)/(2sqrt(3)) distinguish the enriched-order realization from its Ehrhart-equivalent enriched-chain crosspolytope partner (ratio sqrt(n)); these are not furnished by the known Ehrhart/transfer results, and a researcher comparing geometry of enriched poset polytopes could need these exact values. Elementary linear algebra after specialization is transparently acknowledged; no general arbitrary-poset radii claimed.
residual_risks: Specialized simplex computations are elementary and their standalone importance is limited to metric comparison of these canonical realizations.
